title: Integer programming on polytopes of Chvátal rank one is as hard as lattice problems
summary: A rational polyhedron has Chvátal rank at most one if a single round of Chvátal-Gomory cuts yields its integer hull. For such polyhedra, integer feasibility is in NP $\cap$ coNP by a result of Boyd and Pulleyblank from the early 1980s, so it is unlikely to be NP-hard. Whether it is polynomial has remained open since then. We answer this question negatively, under either of two standard assumptions from lattice-based cryptography.
